              How Card Chess works

                One shared deck of 50 cards: in 4 colors, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, Skip, Reverse and +2, plus 2 each of Wild, Wild +4, Swap, Freeze and Shield. The colors are only for looks.                                                                                         RE4 co-op
                                                                                        Play RE4 (2023) with friends through the co-op mod’s Direct Connect, over Tailscale (free, and it gets through any router) instead of the mod’s server. One of you hosts and invites the others. This page checks every part on this PC, backs up your saves and starts the game.
                                                                                        
      
                                                                                        
        
                                                                                        Set up this PC
                                                                                        
        
                                                                                        To host: one button installs Tailscale if it’s missing, blocks the co-op mod’s own server and lets only your friends reach the game’s port. Windows asks for permission once. Then sign in to Tailscale (a Google or Microsoft account works).
                                                                                        
        
                                                                                        Windows Firewall is off on this PC, so the firewall rules won’t do anything until it’s on (Windows Security, Firewall & network protection). If another security app does your firewall, block 2.25.197.34 there.
                                                                                        
        
                                                                                        
        
                                                                                        
          
                                                                                        To join a friend who hosts: paste the invite they sent you. It installs Tailscale if it’s missing and blocks the co-op mod’s own server after one Windows prompt, then opens your host’s share in the browser: sign in to Tailscale there and accept it.

                                                                                        Uses the character swap in ClayBTV’s Multiplayer Mod, no lobby needed: load into your game, pick here, then Direct Connect. Pick once and stay, since every switch reloads the game’s sounds and animations.
                                                                                        
      
                                                                                        Their mod is Multiplayer Mod by ClayBTV, adjusted for Premade so it goes on as Guest by itself and connects you over Direct Connect, and shared here under its Nexus permissions with credit to its creator. If it isn’t in your Downloads, Premade brings the same files from its own site, plus REFramework (MIT) if the game doesn’t have it, and checks every one first.

                                                                                              Friends can join by choosing an open room on the Rooms page, typing this code on the site or in the Windows client, or opening your invite link. Rooms you create are listed while they are active and unlocked. Everyone in the same game should be in the same room.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              How far away you can hear other champions, in game units; 1,350 is about how far a champion sees. It starts at 1,200. Voices fade to silent at the edge, the way Fade says. It only changes what you hear.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              How voices fade as their champions move away; all of them reach silence at the edge of your hearing range. Normal: full volume up to two thirds of the range, then down to silent. Gentle: quieter little by little from close by. Realistic: like real sound, half as loud each time the distance doubles. Sharp: full volume until just before the edge. The dashed ring on the map shows where the fade starts.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Where everyone is in League, as the desktop app sees it: in the client, in a lobby, finding a match, in champ select, loading or in game. Players on the website show as not known, or in game once their minimap is tracked. Before a game everyone hears everyone; with League mode on, once it starts you only hear players close to you on the map.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Sharing your screen lets the page read your minimap and follow your champion's icon, so your camera can roam. It learns which icon is yours from your camera: early in a game, hold Space for a couple of seconds while you walk, or play with the camera locked. If the gold circle isn't on you, press Not my champion. In the Windows client it knows your champion from League itself.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              While you share your screen, everyone in the room sees it in their room, straight from your PC. Games don’t change that: everyone keeps seeing it. You’re told who’s watching. Turn it off and your screen isn’t shown to anyone; you still see theirs. Hide on someone’s screen hides it until you press Show screen on their card.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Only the host can hide the room: whoever made it, or once they leave, the player listed first (their card says host). A hidden room leaves Open voice rooms, and only the friends the host ticks under Who can see it find it there, with a Join button. It also gets a password: friends already in stay in, and anyone joining with just the code has to type it. The invite link and Invite include it, and it stays hidden until everyone leaves. Untick a friend who's in the room and they stay, but the password changes, so they can't come back once they leave. The host can also remove someone, which changes the password the same way. Our server checks the password too, so nobody without it gets through to anyone in the room. The host can also mute a noisy mic for everyone (Mute for all on a card), and that player sees why.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              On: once a League game starts, you hear each other by where your champions are, the room shows the game layout and Game mode works. Off: everyone hears everyone at full volume, in games too, and your shared screen stays as it is. The host picks for everyone, and it stays that way between games. The room Premade makes for a game starts with it on.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The host picks the mode for everyone in the room. It works while League mode (at the top of the room) is on. Classic: proximity chat, nothing else. Legends: your voice changes with the game: deep and booming with Baron, fiery with Elder, your team's dragon soul, a big metal shell with Herald, buzzing with Voidgrubs, crumbling stone when your team takes a tower, a super minion's when it takes an inhibitor, bigger on a killing spree, a cocky echo after a steal, a stadium echo on an Ace, and cheering or gloomy after the game. Immersive: hollow and spooky while dead, watery in the river, a whoosh when you're really fast. Gibberish: the other team comes out as scrambled nonsense. Voice swap: every voice comes from someone else's spot on the map, reshuffled now and then, with a warning first and a reveal after. Showdown: when you and one enemy are alone near each other, everyone else fades, so you hear only each other. Chaos: Legends, Immersive and Gibberish at once. Everything but the river voice and Voice swap needs League's own data, so the desktop app. In Voice swap you can also guess who's behind each voice: right guesses score at each reveal.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Clearer, fuller sound for a good mic with headphones. It turns off the browser's echo cancelling, noise cutting and volume levelling, and sends your voice at 96 kbps instead of 80, which uses a bit more internet. Without headphones, others may hear themselves echo.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              An AI filter (RNNoise) that takes keyboard clicks, fans and background noise out of your mic while keeping your voice. Turn it off if your voice sounds robotic.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Like Discord’s attenuation: while a friend you can hear is talking, every other app’s sound, your game too, goes down by this much, and back up a second after they stop. Unlike Windows’ own setting it only happens while someone talks. Desktop app only.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Others only hear you while your mic is louder than this. Talk normally and watch the bar, then raise the gate until typing and background noise stay below it but your voice doesn't. Or press Set the gate for me and stay quiet for 3 seconds: it listens to your room and puts the gate just above its noise.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Where everyone's voices come out. Using Wave Link? Pick its Voice Chat channel here, the same way you would in Discord.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              When it's on, the app listens to your mic during games for “Premade, clip that” and your own phrase, and saves a clip as the clip key does, even while you're muted. The speech recognition (Vosk) runs on this computer: nothing you say is sent anywhere or kept. The first time it downloads its English speech model, about 40 MB, and during games it takes about 200 MB of memory. Your own phrase: press Record my phrase and say it, or type it, in English, with at least two words you wouldn't say by accident.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Shortcuts need Ctrl, Alt or Shift with a letter, number or F key, so they don't clash with League. The Windows client catches them while League is in front; a browser only while this page is.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              With a push-to-talk key, others only hear you while you hold it. Mouse side buttons work too. In the Windows client it works while League is in front; in a browser only while this page is.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The screen the client shares to read your minimap. Pick the one League is on; the overlay shows up on that screen too.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              A see-through layer on top of League with what you tick here. League must be in Borderless mode (Settings, Video, Window Mode) for anything to show on top of it. In Where it sits, press Edit layout, then drag a part anywhere on your screen, or drag the rest; Put it back returns the part you picked to where it started. Move it on my screen lets you drag the rest on the League screen itself, and size it by its corner. On the loading screen it shows all ten players, like Porofessor: your team on the left at the top, theirs below, with their rank, their record on their champion and tags, and the tips for your lane on the right (app 1.10). In a game, the overlay shortcut (Keys) shows everyone's rank again; press it again to hide the overlay, and once more to bring it back. The CS counter is your CS a minute against your usual on that champion; League only updates it every 10 CS. My lane is your CS and the gold in your items against the player in your lane on the other team.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              For new players, to make glancing at the minimap a habit: “Check your minimap” shows at the top of the screen for 2 seconds, every 10 seconds in your first game with it and a second longer apart each game after that. After 20 games it turns itself off. Summoner's Rift only. It goes by League's clock alone, never by what happens in the game.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              For the first 14 minutes of a Summoner’s Rift game, My lane is a box: each player in your lane (bot: all four, mid and top: you and your lane opponent) with their level, Flash (its time left once it’s timed on the enemy spell strip; yours only while Auto Flash reads your spell keys, your support’s isn’t known), the gold in their items and CS. Below, one line: who hit level 2 first (also at the top of the screen for 5 seconds, read out only with Read them out loud), “Both went back: about 30 s” when their side of the lane went to buy or died, or who’s stronger by levels, Flash and gold in items. League shows no XP, so the level 2 race is known only once someone hits 2. It needs League’s positions, so not in blind pick, and shows only on Summoner’s Rift. With a minimap callout on, it also says when your own jungler walks toward you, like “Jarvan IV coming bot, about 6 s”, never out loud.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              When their jungler drops off your minimap, a small box by League’s minimap says how many seconds you have before they could walk to you: the shortest way round the walls at their move speed (with boots and items), and about a second sooner while their Flash is up on the enemy spell strip. It counts down, turns red under 5 seconds and says “Could be here” at 0, then goes until you see them again. Before you first see them it counts from their fountain at 0:00, and after they buy something out of sight, from their fountain then. With Faded faces on, their faded face gets a grey outline of everywhere they could have walked since, up to 20 seconds. Walls only: it doesn’t know your team’s wards, so it’s on the careful side. Move it moves and sizes the box. Summoner's Rift only.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              For new players, to learn to watch for the other team’s jungler: when their jungler shows up on your minimap, where they are (“Vi at your red”, “Vi in top river”, “Vi in their bot jungle”) shows at the top of the screen for 3 seconds, and again each time they show up after 10 seconds out of sight. Text only, unless Read them out loud (Callouts, Sound) is on. It reads only your minimap from your screen, so it never knows more than you can see. Summoner's Rift only.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Each callout shows at the top of the screen for 3 seconds, the most urgent first. Their jungler heading your way: when your minimap shows their jungler coming toward you. Missing laners: when a player you saw in a lane for a few seconds has been out of sight for 10 seconds, like “Zed missing from mid”. Enemies in your jungle: when they come in, like a level 1 invade, and again after 20 seconds without any. Who’s off your minimap: everyone on their team you can’t see, how long since you last saw them and where they were heading; a dead one shows about when they’re back. In Summoner’s Rift games, Premade reads your minimap from the screen in Settings, League, Screen, by itself, and nothing leaves your computer unless you’re in a voice room. Read them out loud, under Sound, uses your computer’s own voice.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Enemy timers: during a game, say “Premade, mid flash”, “Premade, top ultimate” (top, jungle, mid, bot or support) or “Premade, their red” (or blue), or tap them on your phone remote, and the countdown shows with the objective timers on the overlay, the Game page and your phone, for everyone in your voice room in that game who has them on. Flash takes 5 minutes and an ultimate its cooldown at their level, less the haste in their items; a buff is back 5 minutes after it’s taken. Tap a running one on your phone to take it off. Premade listens for these phrases on your computer, as it does for clips by voice. Power spikes: “Zed is level 6” at levels 6, 11 and 16, and “Jinx finished Infinity Edge”. Coach: a tip now and then at the top of the screen: when you have the gold for the next item of your build (app 1.15), an objective in 60 seconds, 3 or more of them dead (app 1.15), or 2 levels down on your lane opponent. I’m new adds why, and what to do. Jungle clock: at 2:45, where their jungler likely is when their first clear ends, from their own last games and where your minimap first showed them. Enemy timers are in In game, the rest in Callouts, From the game. These show at the top of the screen (app 1.10), and Read them out loud reads them too.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Inhouse ladder: every custom game you play to the end with the desktop app counts, for everyone in it: a rating that goes up when you win and down when you lose, more against a stronger team. Everyone in the room shares the games they have, so the ladder is the same for all of you, and Balance teams uses it once two of the room are on it. Fearless series (Room games, the host starts it): in the custom games after it starts, nobody picks a champion already played in it; champ select shows the ones used up.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              When a game loads, the client joins a room made for that game, so everyone in it with the client hears each other without a code. It never moves you out of a room you joined yourself, or out of a room someone else is in.
                                                                                              


                                                                                               The strongest champions in each role in high elo: the Challenger and Grandmaster ranked games in Korea, Europe West and North America our server counts from Riot, this patch (with the last one added while this one is new). Games from switches to Emerald and Diamond games in Europe West and North America, once our server has some; below Master the list starts on those when a role has enough of them. The tier comes from a champion's win rate, pulled toward 50% while it has few games so a lucky streak doesn't top the list: S, then A, B, C and D. Picked is how many of the games had it in that role. A champion shows once it has 10 games. It starts with S tier (the top 3 when a role has fewer): See more shows every tier. Click one to open its page in that role. An arrow shows a champion rising (▲) or falling (▼) since last patch: its win rate moved more than chance would, with 30 games or more in each patch. Banned is how many of the games had it banned, once our server counts bans.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Try any draft before you queue. Click a slot or Your bans, then one of its faces or any champion. Each role’s 3 faces are its best picks with everything else on the board, and on their side what beats your team. Your bans start with what beats your team most. Fill both laners of a lane for that matchup: the high elo record, runes, first items and tips. Nothing goes to League, and the board hides during a game, as Riot’s rules ask.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The draft: your team on top and theirs below, each champion in its role (theirs are guessed from where each plays in high elo) with its score in this draft, and each team's total. Pick a role between them to rank every champion for it: Meta by its high elo win rate in that role, Matchups by how it does in high elo against their champion in that lane, with your team's champions and against the rest of theirs, plus what your team lacks and your games with your duo, and Balanced by both, plus your own games and mastery on it. For an ADC or a support, Bot lane first counts your lane 4 times the rest of the draft. A score is win rate points above or below 50%, pulled toward what the champions' own win rates would give while there are few games. Click a champion to hover it (or ban it on your ban turn), and again on your turn to lock it in. While their laner isn't picked yet, Matchups and Balanced also count how often the champions they may still pick beat it in that lane, so safe blind picks come first. Right-click one to add it to your favorites, which come first. Type anywhere on this page to find a champion, and Enter hovers the first one. High elo is Korea's Challenger and Grandmaster ranked games our server counts from Riot.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              In a Practice Tool game, the app shows the keys you press on the overlay with the time between them: League's usual keys for your abilities (Q, W, E, R), summoner spells (D, F), items (1 to 7) and right clicks. Keys pressed less than the gap you pick apart make one combo, timed from its first key to its last, and Premade keeps your best time for each combo on each champion. Right clicks show, but moving between casts doesn't make it another combo. Ctrl with a key levels up an ability, so it isn't counted. Premade reads these keys only in Practice Tool games while this is on, the way push to talk reads its key, and keeps only the combos and their times, on this computer.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              In a Practice Tool game, buy a jungle pet and clear your camps: Premade times each camp you finish by League's game clock, from the gold it gives, and saves your clear once you've done the number of camps you pick. Your best clear on each champion with that many camps is the one each camp is held against, like a speedrun, and your clear's time is the game clock when its last camp is done. Practice Tool's gold buttons and selling items don't count as camps, but taking minions or a kill in between does. Needs app 1.15, which tells the page your gold.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              With it on, the app keeps the last part of your main screen (or the one picked in Settings), with what you hear and your mic, in any app or game, not only League, so the clip key and “Premade, clip that” save a clip wherever you are. Clips from outside League are listed here; League’s stay on the Clips page. They use the clip length and the voice settings in Clip settings, on the Clips page. It takes some of your computer’s power all the time. Saying it works in League games and while a game or another app fills your screen: the speech recognition (about 200 MB of memory) loads then and goes 5 minutes after.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Record any screen or app window, like OBS, whenever you like, not only in League: Record (or the Record key, which works while other apps are in front) asks which one, and the same again stops it. It records what you hear, and your mic if you tick it, at the quality and frame rate you pick here (never bigger than the screen or window). It goes in Videos\Premade\Games and is listed on this page, kept until you bin it; it plays here and in any video player, and you can skip around in it and cut it. While Record every match records a game, that game’s video is the recording.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              With Record every match on (the strip at the top of the Clips page), the app records each game you play, except Practice Tool, at the quality and frame rate in Settings, Clips, Recording (it says how big 30 minutes is). It goes in Videos\Premade\Games as it records. Its highlights come from League's own game events (your kills, multikills and deaths, Aces, Dragons, Barons, Heralds, Voidgrubs, towers and inhibitors): click one to watch it right here, Play highlights to watch them one after another, and Save the cut to keep one as a clip. You can also skip around in it in any video player. Videos older than the days you pick go to the Recycle Bin. It records the screen League is on (Settings, League, Screen) with what you hear and your mic, like clips.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Once a game is over: how you played against your usual games on that champion (from your last 100), high elo players on it in your role (Korea's Challenger and Grandmaster games our server counts) and your lane opponent, with what stood out; your gold and CS against your lane opponent minute by minute; where you got kills and died; the objectives each team took; then everyone's score, your laning and when everyone bought each item. From Riot's match history and the game's timeline. Riot doesn't allow advice during a game, so it comes after.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Your phone as a remote for League, on any network, while this app is open on your PC: scan the code with your phone’s camera, or Copy link and open it there. It follows League one screen at a time, in your colours: pick the game and your roles, invite friends and find a match; accept it; go through champ select (picks for you, trades, runes, spells, skins and dodge); and in a game see the score, the objectives and your lane, time their Flash and ultimates and call them missing. Chat has your room’s chat and League chat. It buzzes and rings when a match is found or it’s your turn while the page is open; turn on “Tell me when a match is found” in its Settings for a notification even with its screen off (on an iPhone, open the remote from its home screen icon first). Anyone with the link can use it, so keep it to yourself; New code makes a fresh one.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The desktop app talks to League's own client on this PC, through the local connection League offers apps. It never reads the game's memory. Accept matches for me waits a moment, then accepts every match found while the app runs. Hover for me hovers the first champion on your list that's free and fits your role as soon as champ select starts, and your ban on your ban turn; you still lock in yourself.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Games for the whole room, started by the host. Balance teams: two even teams for a custom game, from the inhouse ladder once two of the room are on it (Customs, below), else from everyone's Solo/Duo rank (shared by the desktop app with League; anyone whose rating or rank isn't known counts as the room's average). Role roulette: a random role each, different within each team; in the desktop app, one click puts yours first in League's lobby. Best roles: the same, but each player gets the role they win most in, from their recent Summoner's Rift games (shared by the desktop app with League; a role played fewer than 10 times counts for less). MVP vote: after a game with friends in voice everyone votes for the MVP, and the winner wears a crown on their card next game; the host can also start one. Mock draft: practice a Clash-style draft, bans and picks, 30 seconds a turn; anyone on the side whose turn it is can choose. Room awards come after each game with friends in voice, from talk time and League's scoreboard. Fearless series: custom games where nobody picks a champion already played in the series; champ select shows the ones used up (Customs, below).
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Tags come from the last 20 games, mastery, level and Riot's ranked flags. Green and red ones are good to know, gold ones are just for fun. A few (kill participation, solo kills, steals, pings) are only in Riot's own match data, so they don't show for games from League's client. Past ranks: League's client tells the desktop app where last season ended and its peak, and this season's peak, for players on your server, and the app keeps yours for when League is closed. Riot doesn't give older seasons, so our server keeps every rank it gets from Riot, season by season, and shows those seasons once they're over. Nothing from other sites.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Tap a champion to put it on your board, and tap it on the board to take it out. Tap a trait to see only its champions. Copy team code gives TFT’s Team Planner this board; Paste code loads a code you copied. A code holds up to 10 champions, not their items, and only works in the set it was made for.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              The bars are what a shop slot rolls at your level. The rings are your chance of the 2 and 3 star with your gold: each roll costs 2, and the copies you still need are kept back to buy. Copies other players hold of other champions aren’t known, so it’s a little hopeful.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Tap a component to see the items it makes. A gold ring means you built that item in your last 20 games.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Newest first, from League’s client on this PC. Traits count when they were on in that game.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              During a game the app keeps the last part of the screen League is on in memory, with what you hear and your mic. The clip key, saying “Premade, clip that” (Settings, Clips), a double kill or a big moment saves it as a video in Videos\Premade; nothing is saved otherwise. Clips are .mp4, which phones, WhatsApp and Discord play; the first one is .webm while the app fetches FFmpeg to make them. Each game is a row with its clips. Here you can play, cut, rename and save your clips, copy one to paste into a chat, or drag one straight into Discord. Saved clips stay in their game (press Saved to see only them) and are never binned when the folder gets too big. Recording takes some of your computer's power: 720p, 30 fps or turning clips off helps if League stutters. Quality is never more than your screen's size.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Faster sends your friends' voices to you in smaller pieces, so they arrive a little sooner; it uses a bit more internet. Less data sends fewer, bigger pieces at a lower quality, both ways, for anyone on slow internet. Changing it reconnects voice for a moment. Whatever you pick, when a friend starts losing some of your voice on the way, it goes to them in lower quality by itself until that stops, without reconnecting.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Saves what League tells the app during each game (its game data and what champ select and match history said) in Documents\Premade\Test recordings, with every name and account id swapped for Player 1, Player 2 and so on. No voice and no video. Send one to whoever builds the app so new features get tried on a real game. The newest 20 are kept.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Everyone in the room who picked a rank goal in the desktop app (Stats, You: Goal), and how close they are: the LP to go, and a bar from where they were when they picked it. It’s shared like your rank, unless that’s off in Settings, League.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Your League friends’ messages and party invites, through League’s own client: read and answer them here or on the phone remote, and accept or decline an invite. With Show my Premade room on, your League status says “Premade room KAYN” while you’re in a room, and your old status comes back when you leave.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              In Discord: Server Settings, Integrations, Webhooks, New Webhook. Pick the channel, press Copy Webhook URL and paste it here. Then after each game Premade posts your result there, with your LP and any rank-up, and each clip you save under 10 MB, straight from this PC. Anyone with the link can post in that channel, so keep it to yourself.
                                                                                              

                                                                                              Back up saves your settings, matchup notes, LP history, game history, reports and clip favorites in one file. Restore loads such a file, on this PC or another, and replaces what's here.
